source_title: GTA 6 Officially Reveals New Details About Jason + Lucia's Criminal Profiles
source_excerpt:
GTA 6 will let players decide just how ruthless they want to be as criminals, with Rockstar Games introducing a new system that will have consequences for Jason and Lucia's story . Whether it's robbing businesses, stealing cars, or getting into shootouts with the police, the Grand Theft Auto series has always been about giving players freedom, especially when it comes to causing chaos throughout its open worlds. However, players haven't always had much reason to think about the consequences of their criminal behavior.
Interestingly, GTA 6 is taking some inspiration from Red Dead Redemption 2 , which introduced a more meaningful approach to player decisions. Arthur Morgan's Honor system tracked his actions throughout the game, with good and bad decisions influencing how characters treated him and even affecting the story's ending. GTA 6 is building on that idea, although the new system is more focused on how players approach a life of crime than the Honor system.
Rockstar has confirmed ( in an interview with Edge Magazine ) that GTA 6 introduces a Criminal Profile system, which tracks Jason and Lucia's behavior on a scale ranging from "Professional" to "Irredeemable." Represented by angel and devil icons, the system determines what kind of criminals players become based on their actions throughout the game. Players who take a more calculated approach can build a professional reputation, while those who consistently resort to violence move toward the other end of the scale. More importantly, Rockstar has confirmed that these decisions will influence how GTA 6's story unfolds , meaning the Criminal Profile system isn't just for show .
Find the odd one out before the timer hits zero.
One of the biggest changes involves GTA 6 's combat , as it won't always require players to kill their enemies. Instead, Jason and Lucia can incapacitate opponents, use threats, or attempt to intimidate people before resorting to violence. Of course, there's nothing stopping players from shooting their way through an encounter, but doing so will contribute to a more violent Criminal Profile.
It's an interesting addition to GTA 6 , particularly considering how many missions throughout the franchise have traditionally ended in shootouts. Now, players may have more reasons to approach certain situations carefully, especially if their decisions could affect what happens later in the story. The Criminal Profile system also ties into Rockstar's broader efforts to make GTA 6 's open world and gameplay more reactive to player decisions. The developer has already confirmed improvements to NPC behavior, police responses, and the freedom players have when completing missions. Some objectives feature multiple routes, while other encounters can transition into the game's open-world systems instead of forcing players down a specific path.
Combined with the ability to threaten or incapacitate enemies, the Criminal Profile system could make GTA 6 feel considerably less restrictive than previous entries. However, Rockstar hasn't explained exactly how the system changes the story, or whether it affects individual missions, dialogue, or the game's ending, nor is it expected to before launch. Either way, the possibility of different story outcomes based on how players commit crimes is a major development for GTA 6 .
